title: 22. Numeracy & Number Systems: Integer Subtraction Using Number Lines
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the result of subtracting a positive integer by moving left on a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(5\) and move \(3\) units to the left. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a positive integer means moving left on a number line. Starting at \(5\) and moving \(3\) units left gives \(5 - 3 = 2\). Therefore, you land on \(2\).
questions.hint: Subtracting a positive integer moves the position to the left.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the result of subtracting a positive integer from a negative integer on a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(-2\) and move \(4\) units to the left. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a positive integer means moving left on a number line. Starting at \(-2\) and moving \(4\) units left gives \(-2 - 4 = -6\). Therefore, you land on \(-6\).
questions.hint: Moving left from a negative integer makes the value smaller.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a subtraction expression involving a negative integer and a positive integer using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(-3 - 5\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-3\) on the number line. Subtracting \(5\) means moving \(5\) units to the left: \(-3 - 5 = -8\). Therefore, the result is \(-8\).
questions.hint: Start at the first integer, then move left for the positive number being subtracted.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret subtraction of a negative integer as moving right on a number line.
questions.question: What is \(4 - (-2)\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a negative integer is the same as adding its opposite. Since \(-(-2) = +2\), start at \(4\) and move \(2\) units to the right: \(4 - (-2) = 6\). Therefore, the result is \(6\).
questions.hint: Subtracting a negative integer moves the position to the right.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the subtraction expression that represents moving left from a given integer.
questions.question: Which expression represents starting at \(-1\) and moving \(4\) units to the left on a number line?
questions.explanation: Moving to the left on a number line means subtracting a positive integer. Starting at \(-1\) and moving \(4\) units left is represented by \(-1 - 4\). Therefore, the correct expression is \(-1 - 4\).
questions.hint: Moving left makes the value smaller. Which kind of number, when subtracted, makes a value smaller?

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate subtraction of a negative integer using a number line.
questions.question: What is \(-5 - (-3)\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Subtracting \(-3\) is the same as adding \(3\). Start at \(-5\) and move \(3\) units to the right: \(-5 - (-3) = -2\). Therefore, the result is \(-2\).
questions.hint: Subtracting a negative integer is equivalent to moving to the right.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the subtraction expression that describes a move from one integer to another.
questions.question: On a number line, a move starts at \(2\) and ends at \(-3\). Which subtraction expression describes this move?
questions.explanation: The move starts at \(2\) and ends at \(-3\), so the position decreases by \(5\). Moving \(5\) units left represents subtracting \(5\). Therefore, the expression is \(2 - 5\).
questions.hint: Compare the starting and ending positions to decide whether the move is left or right.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a subtraction expression by moving left from a positive integer.
questions.question: What is \(3 - 7\) using a number line?
questions.explanation: Start at \(3\) on the number line. Subtracting \(7\) means moving \(7\) units to the left: \(3 - 7 = -4\). Therefore, the result is \(-4\).
questions.hint: Start at the first integer. In which direction do you move when a positive integer is subtracted? Notice that you will pass \(0\).

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a multi-step integer subtraction using a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(-4\), subtract \(6\), and then subtract \(-2\). Where do you end?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-4\). Subtract \(6\) by moving \(6\) units left: \(-4 - 6 = -10\). Then subtract \(-2\), which means moving \(2\) units right: \(-10 - (-2) = -8\). Therefore, you end at \(-8\).
questions.hint: Perform the moves one at a time in the order given.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret the meaning of subtracting a negative integer on a number line.
questions.question: Which description matches \(6 - (-8)\) on a number line?

options.label: A
options.text: Start at \(6\) and move \(8\) units to the left.

options.label: B
options.text: Start at \(6\) and move \(8\) units to the right.

questions.explanation: The expression \(6 - (-8)\) means subtracting negative \(8\). Subtracting a negative integer is the same as adding its opposite, so \(6 - (-8) = 6 + 8\). On a number line, this means starting at \(6\) and moving \(8\) units to the right. Therefore, the correct description is to start at \(6\) and move \(8\) units to the right.
questions.hint: Rewrite \(6 - (-8)\) as an addition, then decide which direction that addition moves on the number line.
